chunks: He said, "O Noah, truly he is not of your family. He is surely the outcome of an unrighteous act. So ask Me not of what you do not know. I warn you not to be one of the ignorant."
ai.seo_question: Why was Noah's son not considered part of his family in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this verse, God addresses Noah (AS) with the phrase 'innahu min ahlika' (he is indeed of your family) before correcting it with 'innahu 'amalun ghayru saliḥ' (his deed was not righteous), highlighting the Shia scholarly distinction between biological lineage and spiritual merit. This moment underscores the principle that piety (taqwa) is the true criterion for inclusion in the divine family, a concept central to Shia exegesis regarding the Ahl al-Bayt. The admonition 'la tas'alni ma laysa laka bihi 'ilm' serves as a broader lesson on accepting divine wisdom even when it seems to contradict human emotional attachment.
